name: Shi Da Cha
parentage: A local, large-leaf mutation of C. sinensis var. sinensis.
description: 'Persimmon Big Tea'. A truly unique and visually stunning cultivar from Taiping county in Anhui. It is defined by its massive leaves, which can be much larger than a person's hand. It is used exclusively to make Tai Ping Hou Kui, a green tea where the leaves are painstakingly pressed by hand, resulting in a long, flat, and beautiful finished product.
plantType: Large, robust bush with very strong branches to support its massive leaves (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows in the misty, mountainous region of the former Taiping prefecture (now Huangshan district), where the specific microclimate allows these large leaves to grow tenderly.
processing: The processing is highly specialized and laborious. After kill-green, each individual leaf is placed between layers of cloth and hand-pressed with rollers to create its flat, uniform shape. This requires immense patience and skill.
oxidation: Zero oxidation. The massive leaves are quickly pan-fired to halt enzymatic activity and preserve their vibrant green color and fresh aroma.
roasting: A gentle baking process follows the hand-pressing to slowly and evenly dry the large, thick leaves without scorching them or creating a roasted flavor.
versatility: Completely specialized. This unique, giant-leaf cultivar exists only to be made into the singular and iconic Tai Ping Hou Kui.

china: Anhui Province (Huangshan City - former Taiping County area)

Green Tea.Tai Ping Hou Kui ('Peaceful Monkey Leade: Its only expression. A green tea where individual, massive leaves are pan-fired and then pressed flat between layers of cloth, creating a visually unique tea with a powerful orchid aroma.

sensory.aroma: Powerful and lingering Orchid fragrance, fresh, clean, and slightly vegetal
sensory.flavor: Mellow, sweet, and smooth with a deep, lasting floral sweetness and no bitterness.
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Thick, soupy, and incredibly smooth with a very refreshing character. The liquor is a clear, bright green-yellow.
